statement: The no-bypass meta-check (H00-1.1, crates/enforcer-security/src/rules/no_bypass.rs) is the one validator in the workspace that must NOT apply the standard comment-only-line guard (the pattern documented in enforcer-lang-security's text_scan module doc and used by every other line-scan validator here). Every other rule treats a banned pattern MENTIONED in a comment as a non-occurrence; for no-bypass, the violation IS a comment/attribute (`// eslint-disable`, `# noqa`, `@ts-ignore`, `#[allow(...)]`), so guarding out comment lines would make the check permanently silent.
why: Discovered while implementing the skeleton: copying the secret_scan.rs/generic_scanner.rs comment-guard pattern verbatim would have produced a validator that compiles, has green unit tests using non-comment marker text, but is structurally incapable of ever firing on its real target (inline suppress directives are always inside a comment or attribute).
howToApply: Any Track H feature pack (h01-h08, h11) or future security-testing validator whose target IS a comment/annotation shape (suppression directives, waiver-adjacent markers, doc-only policy claims) should default to scanning every line unconditionally and only add narrower guards (e.g. skip inside a raw string literal) if a real false-positive surfaces in a fixture -- do not reflexively import the is_comment_only_line guard from enforcer-lang-security.

statement: There is no `H0*`/`H1*`-prefixed rule family in rules/rules.json yet (only the pre-existing `security` family used by enforcer-lang-security's SEC-1/SEC-2 rows). The no-bypass meta-check's rule id `H00-1.1` was newly minted by this workpack (arc-19) following the `PREFIX-N.N` shape enforcer_domain::ids::RuleId requires, and is NOT yet a row in rules/rules.json -- the arc-19 skeleton's own completeness test (tests/completeness.rs) deliberately does NOT do a rules.json family-count-parity check like enforcer-lang-security's, because the Track H money-critical (h01-h08) and security-testing (h11) feature packs will add their own rule ids/registry rows on top of this skeleton, and a rules.json-count-locked test here would break the moment the first feature pack lands.
why: Avoided copying enforcer-lang-security's completeness.rs pattern (which asserts registry count == rules.json family count == 22) verbatim, since that would make arc-19's own test suite red as soon as sibling h0x packs start registering rows without also editing arc-19-owned files (which they must not touch).
howToApply: Feature packs landing rows into crates/enforcer-security/src/rules/registry.rs::build_all should mint their own rules/rules.json entries with `family` values appropriate to Track H (money-critical/security-testing, TBD exact family string) and should NOT expect arc-19's tests/completeness.rs to enforce that linkage for them -- if a Track H family-wide count-parity gate is wanted later, a feature pack (or a later doc pass) should add it explicitly once the full rule set is known.

evidence.ref: rules/rules.json has no H00/H01../money-critical family rows as of arc-19; crates/enforcer-security/tests/completeness.rs scoped to duplicate-check + H00-1.1 presence only
